attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The present-tense, unhedged claim that GPT models on their own don't do scientific discovery is fairly treated as an observation. The 'on their own' qualifier is kept. The nearby 'always will be' line is about making things up, not discovery, so leaving it out is correct.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: a new, independently checked finding, with the model doing the essential work. Limiting it to models that existed by the post date fits the present tense. The autonomy and novelty thresholds are vague, but they don't decide the result here, because the evidence settles neither side.

evidence.note: A 2023 retrospective by one researcher says ChatGPT could not yet do science alone and gave poor mathematical physics. This is one person's experiment, not a broad assessment of GPT capability by April 2023, and later revisions muddy its dating. It cannot meet the support condition alone.

The Sparks of AGI preprint (22 March 2023) shows GPT-4 producing a correct proof of an existing problem, with human prompting. That is a capability result, not a novel, independently validated discovery made by the model alone, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: Neither condition is met. The support condition needs credible broad assessments that examined purported discoveries. The packet has only one researcher's anecdotal account (e1) and a capability demo (e2). No item shows a validated novel finding by a GPT model on its own by 8 April 2023, so the claim is not contradicted. The possibly relevant 7 April hypothesis paper could not be read. The evidence leaves the outcome unsettled.
